paper: Autor, Dorn, Hanson (2013 AER) 'The China Syndrome: Local Labor Market Effects of Import Competition in the United States'
summary: All 10 replication steps executed successfully in Python (pandas + linearmodels), reimplementing the authors' Stata do-files. Every reproduced coefficient matches the authors' shipped Stata logs to 3 decimal places; SEs match to ~0.001 (minor cluster df-adjustment difference between Stata ivregress and linearmodels debiased clustered VCE). No downsizing: all regressions run at full scale (N=1444 CZ x period, or the period-specific N).
validation_method: Reproduced values compared against the authors' shipped Stata .scsv/.log files in codebase/log/ and against paper claims. See per-step notes.

step_outcomes.description: Set up environment, validate inputs, build reusable weighted-2SLS helper with state-clustered SEs.
step_outcomes.command_executed: uv venv; uv pip install pandas numpy scipy linearmodels statsmodels openpyxl xlrd matplotlib; python -c 'read_stata workfile_china.dta'
step_outcomes.notes: workfile_china.dta shape (1444, 208) = 722 CZs x 2 periods, confirmed. All required variables present (d_sh_empl_mfg, d_tradeusch_pw, d_tradeotch_pw_lag, timepwt48, statefip, l_shind_manuf_cbp, l_sh_popedu_c, l_sh_popfborn, l_sh_empl_f, l_sh_routine33, l_task_outsource, t2, and 8 reg_* dummies). Helper repro/iv.py implements iv2sls (Stata ivregress 2sls [aw], cluster), ols (Stata reg [aw], cluster), and a Stata-style weighted percentile. Validated: Table 3 col1 coef -0.746/se 0.069 (Stata -0.746/0.068), col6 coef -0.596/se 0.100 (Stata -0.596/0.099).

step_outcomes.description: Table 1 trade statistics + Figure 1 time series.
step_outcomes.notes: US imports from China: 26.27/121.56/330.02 bn USD (12.6x growth 1991-2007); US exports to China: 10.32/23.00/57.41 bn USD (5.6x) -- import growth far exceeds export growth. China share of low-income mfg imports = usch/(usch+uslw): 0.774(1991)->0.879(2007); China share of the 2000-2007 GROWTH in low-income imports = 0.902, matching the paper's stated ~89%. Figure 1: import penetration (impr) 0.6%(1991)->4.7%(2007); mfg emp/pop (cpsmanufemppop) 12.6%->8.4% -- both EXACT matches to the paper's Figure 1 text. Note: mfg-emp/pop series column is named 'cpsmanufemppop' in figure1_data.dta (the do-file's 'cpsman').
